facts.statement: Xiangornis is a member of the Enantiornithes clade of birds.
facts.quote: Xiangornis is an enantiornithean bird from the Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Western Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: A fossil of this bird was discovered in 2005 near Dapingfang in Chaoyang, Western Liaoning.
facts.quote: In 2005, a bird fossil was discovered near Dapingfang in Chaoyang, in Western Liaoning.

facts.statement: The species Xiangornis shenmi was named and described in 2012 by Hu Dongyu, Xu Xing, Hou Lianhai, and Corwin Sullivan.
facts.quote: The type species Xiangornis shenmi was in 2012 named and described by Hu Dongyu, Xu Xing, Hou Lianhai and Corwin Sullivan.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, PMOL-AB00245, dates to the Aptian stage, approximately 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, PMOL-AB00245, had been found in the Jiufotang Formation dating from the Aptian, about 120 million years old.

facts.statement: The holotype fossil consists of a left wing along with parts of the shoulder girdle and sternum.
facts.quote: It consists of the left wing and adjacent parts of the shoulder girdle and the sternum.

facts.statement: Xiangornis shenmi belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
Xiangornis lived during the Aptian stage, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
